summary: The blueprint broadly covers healthy human pancreas, but targeted vascular, mural/stromal, and ductal marker refinements would make it more biologically complete.

issues.description: Blood endothelial cells are mostly represented as one broad vascular axis plus a lymphatic refinement, so capillary/fenestrated/islet endothelial, arterial, and venous/postcapillary endothelial programs may collapse into one dimension.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one or more gated endothelial subtype axes under a pan-endothelial gate, such as capillary/fenestrated/islet endothelial markers PLVAP, EMCN, RAMP2, RGCC, CA4; arterial markers GJA5, SOX17, EFNB2, HEY1; and/or venous/postcapillary markers ACKR1, VWF, SELE, VCAM1.

issues.description: The pericyte/smooth muscle axis is gated by a fibroblast/ECM-heavy mesenchymal module, which could suppress true mural cells that express RGS5, PDGFRB, CSPG4, NOTCH3, ACTA2, TAGLN, or MYH11 but not strong fibroblast markers.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a broader mural/mesenchymal gate, or make the mural program a plain axis/contrast separate from fibroblast-stellate identity. If gated, the gate should include mural-compatible markers rather than only fibroblast ECM markers.

issues.description: Pancreatic stellate/fibroblast biology is represented mainly by ECM-remodeling genes, which captures activated matrix-producing states but under-resolves quiescent pancreatic stellate and vitamin-A/lipid-associated stellate biology expected in healthy pancreas.
issues.suggested_fix: Add or revise a stellate/quiescent module with markers such as RGS5, PDGFRB, DES, LRAT, RBP1, PDPN, and COL15A1 as appropriate, and contrast it against the matrix-remodeling/activated fibroblast program.

issues.description: The ductal module is usable but blends baseline ductal transport markers with TFF1/TFF2 and SPP1, which can emphasize mucinous/metaplastic or injury-associated ductal programs and may bias a healthy baseline ductal identity axis.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep core ductal markers such as KRT19, KRT7, SOX9, CFTR, SLC4A4, SLC26A6, MUC1, ANXA4, and HNF1B; move TFF1/TFF2 and possibly high SPP1 emphasis into a separate reactive/mucinous ductal state axis if desired, or replace them with more baseline ductal markers such as KRT17, KRT23, MMP7, ANXA4, or HNF1B.

out_of_scope: Endocrine epsilon cells are rare in adult pancreas, but age is unspecified here, so retaining an epsilon axis is reasonable.
Immune subtyping is broad but acceptable for a healthy whole-pancreas embedding; deeper immune-state resolution is optional rather than required.
